title: Decide which render requests wait for a renderer

blocks.text: The PDF render farm has a fixed number of renderers, shared by two kinds of work. Interactive previews come from users looking at a spinner. Batch documents come from the nightly scheduler, which retries anything refused a few minutes later and runs on a small thread pool of its own.

Last night a slow font server made every render take a minute. The scheduler's threads all ended up parked inside `batch(...)`, so it stopped scheduling anything, including the jobs that don't render at all. Users complained too: some previews spun until the browser gave up, and others were turned away while documents nobody was looking at were being rendered.

Finish `admitPreview()` and `admitBatch()` in `src/main/java/practice/RenderAdmission.java`. `preview(...)` and `batch(...)` already render and give the renderer back. When you're done, a preview waits for a renderer, but no longer than `previewWaitMillis`; a batch document never waits, and never takes a renderer that another caller is already queued for. About two lines in total.
The tests hand the class its semaphore, so they can hold renderers, queue callers, and play a second scheduler that takes a renderer at an awkward moment.

cases.says: with renderers free, previews and batch documents are rendered and every renderer is free again afterwards
a batch document returns at once even when another caller takes the last renderer between a look at the count and the take
a batch document is refused at once when every renderer is busy, without waiting as a preview would
a batch document does not take a free renderer while another caller is queued for renderers
a preview waits for a renderer that frees up within its wait, and renders
a preview gives up and returns false once its wait has passed

origin.section: When the Permits Run Out, Choose: Wait, Wait a Bounded Time, or Refuse

concepts: acquire() waits without bound, tryAcquire(timeout) waits a bounded time, tryAcquire() decides at once; checking availablePermits() before acquire() is a race.
The untimed tryAcquire() takes a free permit even when threads are queued on a fair semaphore; tryAcquire(0, SECONDS) respects the queue.
